readerTitle: The money that comes back without asking
caseNote: 일상 관찰 (개인 통장 내역) + 가상 사례 (상업용 청소 회사, 베이커리, 사진 편집 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 매출의 크기보다, 아무것도 하지 않았을 때 다음 달에도 그 돈이 들어오는지를 본다. 반복 매출은 '계속'이 기본값이고 일회성 매출은 '중단'이 기본값이다.
misconception: 1년 매출 합계가 같으면 같은 사업이다. 단골 손님이 자주 오면 그것이 반복 매출이다.

sources.text: 사업 모델의 표준 개념 (반복 매출과 일회성 매출의 구분)

factChecks.note: 청소 회사 계산: 월 $700 × 12개월 = $8,400로, 일회성 $9,000보다 $600 적습니다. 3번 카드의 월별 금액(1달 차 $9,000 / $0, 계약 $700 / $700)이 2번 카드와 맞는지 다시 확인하세요.
"인수자와 대출 기관이 예측 가능한 수입을 가진 사업에 더 높은 가치를 매기는 경우가 많다"는 일반적 경향으로만 적었습니다. 구체적인 배수나 통계는 넣지 않았습니다.
사진 앱의 $60 일회성 가격과 월 $5 요금은 가상 수치입니다. 실제 기업 사례(예: Adobe)는 BMO-06-09와 겹치지 않도록 일부러 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Some money arrives before anyone decides anything.
body: Look at last month's bank statement. The phone bill, the insurance, the gym. You didn't choose to pay them again. They just came.
Other charges, like a haircut or a new kettle, happened only because you decided to buy, again. For a business, that small difference changes almost everything.

image.label: A bank statement with some lines repeating every month
image.brief: 책상 위 종이 은행 거래 내역서 클로즈업. 'Phone', 'Insurance', 'Gym' 줄은 매달 같은 날짜에 반복되고 순환 화살표 아이콘으로 표시. 'Haircut', 'Kettle' 줄은 한 번씩만 나타나고 점 아이콘으로 표시. 실제 은행, 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: One open slot, two clients.
body: You run a commercial cleaning company with room for one more client this year.

Client A wants a one-time deep clean after an office renovation: **$9,000**, paid this month. Client B wants weekly cleaning at **$700 a month**, cancel with 30 days' notice. Which is worth more to your business?

options.text: Client A. More money, sooner, and no risk of cancelling
options.feedback: You get $9,000 now and a clean finish. But when the job ends, next month starts at zero and you have to sell again.

options.text: Client B. Less this year, but it keeps coming
options.feedback: If they stay 12 months, that's $8,400, a bit less than A. But each month arrives without a new sale, so you can plan staff around it.

options.text: Whichever leaves more profit after labor and supplies
options.feedback: A sensible test, and it matters. But it treats both as the same kind of money, and they aren't.

choice.afterReveal: The yearly totals are close. The real difference is what happens next month if nobody does anything.

cards.title: Look at month two.
body: Winning each client took about the same effort. They leave you in very different places for month two.

breakdown.label: Client A, month 2
breakdown.detail: Only if you win new work

cards.title: Recurring vs one-time revenue
body: **Recurring revenue** comes again without a new sale. The customer has agreed to keep paying, so continuing is the default and stopping takes a decision.
**One-time revenue** ends with the sale. To earn it again, you have to win it again.
A simple test: if you did nothing next month, would the money still come?

image.label: Two paths: a loop that returns and a line that stops
image.brief: 좌우 분할 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 'Recurring': 동전이 원형 고리를 따라 계속 돌아오는 모습, 라벨 'Continues unless someone stops it'. 오른쪽 'One-time': 동전 하나가 직선을 따라 가다가 끝에서 멈춤, 라벨 'Ends unless you sell again'. 단순한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: Why the same dollar isn't worth the same.
body: A one-time business starts every month at zero. A recurring business starts with last month's customers already paying. That changes how you run it:
list: **Planning:** you can hire or buy equipment against income you can see coming
**Selling:** each new client adds to the base instead of replacing last month's work
**Value:** buyers and lenders often value predictable income more highly
cards.callout: One-time revenue runs to stand still. Recurring revenue builds.

cards.title: A regular is not a subscription.
body: A bakery regular who comes in every morning brings repeat revenue. It feels recurring. But every visit is a fresh choice, and a new café next door can end it without notice.
Revenue sits on a spectrum: one-time (a wedding cake), repeat (the daily croissant), recurring (a weekly bread order for a restaurant, billed monthly). Only the last one continues by default.

image.label: Three bakery items on a scale from one-time to recurring
image.brief: 가로 스펙트럼 막대. 왼쪽부터 웨딩 케이크('One-time'), 크루아상 한 개('Repeat'), 매주 배달되는 빵 상자와 달력('Recurring'). 오른쪽으로 갈수록 순환 화살표가 진해짐. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: Recurring revenue is earned again every month.
body: A contract lasts only as long as the customer keeps getting something. Stop delivering, and the default flips to cancel.
It also costs cash early. $700 a month brings in less than $9,000 now, while your own bills still arrive on time.
And some needs really are one-time. Nobody wants a subscription to moving house. Forcing one just adds friction.

cards.title: Now it's a photo app.
body: You sell a photo-editing app for a one-time **$60**. Sales are steady, but every month starts from zero. You're thinking about moving to **$5 a month**.

options.text: Switch everyone to $5 a month and stop selling the $60 version
options.feedback: You'd gain predictable income, but people who edit a few photos a year would pay more for the same app. Many may feel pushed and leave.

options.text: Keep the $60 version and add a $5 monthly plan with ongoing extras, like cloud backup and new tools
options.feedback: The payment recurs because the value recurs. Users get a reason to keep paying, and one-time buyers aren't forced out.

options.text: Keep only the $60 price and spend more on finding new buyers
options.feedback: Simple and fair for people who want to own the app. But income stays a treadmill: each month's sales must be won from scratch.

cards.title: Ask what happens next month if you do nothing.
body: Recurring revenue continues by default. One-time revenue has to be won again. Equal totals can hide very different businesses.
**Try it today:** split last month's revenue into two piles: money that will come again without a new sale, and money you'll have to win again. How big is the first pile?
